<reason>Side A won by sustaining a decisive land-use arithmetic showing that permanent burial plots create infinite spatial demands on finite urban land, effectively answering B's challenge about housing versus green space by clarifying that the goal is to halt cemetery expansion rather than convert existing grounds. While Side B mounted a compelling defense of religious dignity and immediate working-class access, A's counter that "physics is non-negotiable" and that permanent plots eventually exclude everyone when capacity vanishes provided a stronger long-term framework for spatial justice. A's pressure questions forced B into vague capacity answers, and A's direct A1/A2 responses in Rebuttal 2 cleanly resolved the central clash.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 (A4.1) clarified the perceived contradiction in their land-use argument—explaining that the transition stops cemetery footprint expansion rather than converting cemeteries to housing—which defused B's strongest attack from Rebuttal 1 while maintaining the core arithmetic that permanent plots consume land indefinitely.</best_rebuttal>
